HOME_FAQ: Do I need an IEC to export from India?
Yes. Commercial exports need the 10-character Importer-Exporter Code from DGFT, linked to your PAN. The government fee is ₹500 and it is issued online. Our desk can file it for you.
How much money do I need to start exporting?

Set-up is cheap: the IEC fee, your export council's RCMC fee and a digital signature. The real cost is working capital for the first order, which advance payment, a letter of credit or pre-shipment credit can cover. Checking your product here is free.
Which product and which country are best for export from India?

It depends on your HS code. We score 66 countries for your product on market size, growth, how much they already buy from India and the duty they charge on Indian goods, and show the top five with the reason for each.
What documents are needed to export?

A proforma and commercial invoice, packing list, shipping bill (filed by your CHA on ICEGATE), bill of lading or airway bill, the certificate of origin your trade deal needs, and any product certificate. After payment the bank issues the e-BRC.
How do I get a certificate of origin for UAE CEPA or the India–UK CETA?

For the UAE, apply on DGFT Trade Connect and an authorised agency issues the CEPA certificate. For the UK, the exporter completes the CETA origin declaration, or gets a certificate of origin from an Indian issuing authority. We pre-fill the data for you.
What is the UK import duty on my product after the India–UK FTA?

The India–UK CETA came into force on 15 July 2026 and cut duty to 0% on many lines for Indian goods. Leather footwear, for example, went from 8% to 0%. Check your exact HS code on our UK page or upload an invoice.
How do I find genuine buyers and avoid fake ones?

Start with importers who already import your HS code: the UK publishes them through HMRC, and our desk verifies shipment records elsewhere. Check the company registration, never ship on open credit to a new buyer, and confirm any change of bank details by phone.
How will I get paid, and what if the buyer does not pay?
Use advance payment, a letter of credit confirmed by your bank, or ECGC export credit insurance. Our desk checks LC documents before you ship so the bank does not refuse them.
Who pays the customs duty: the exporter or the importer?

The importer pays duty and import VAT in their country. You quote FOB (your price at the Indian port) or CIF (including freight and insurance). Most countries charge duty on CIF; the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand charge it on an FOB-based value.
Do I need GST registration to export?
Yes, for most goods. File a Letter of Undertaking (LUT) to export without paying IGST, or pay IGST and claim the refund.
Do I need an RCMC, and from which council?
Yes, to claim export incentives and join buyer-seller meets. It comes from the export promotion council for your product, for example CLE for leather, AEPC for apparel, the Spices Board or EEPC.
Do I stay the exporter, and what do you charge?
Yes. You stay the exporter of record with your own IEC, buyer and refunds. The self-serve tools are free; the export desk charges per shipment, from ₹12,000 plus GST, with no subscription.
